You receive 4 images. Image 1 is the LAYOUT SKETCH of the finished 1920x1080 game screen: a crude flat-colour blocking that fixes the exact composition - camera, horizon, wall and floor lines, and the position, size and outline of every object. Repaint image 1 into a finished painting: keep every line and every block exactly where it is and exactly as large as it is, paint each block as the object described below, do not move, enlarge, shrink, add or remove anything, and leave no flat colour areas or hard geometric edges. Images 2-3 are photos of the real place (geography, architecture, materials and real details to paint from; they are references only, do not copy their camera, cars, people, signs or weather). Image 4 is a finished background painting from our game: use it ONLY as the reference for the painting technique (brushwork, palette, edge softness, level of detail, line quality); do not copy anything from its scene.

Place: the anteroom of grandmother Mira's old garden workshop, a small red-brick outbuilding standing in the street line of her property in the old core of Čierna Voda (municipality Chorvátsky Grob, near Bratislava, Slovakia). Image 2 is a photo of a real Czech home workshop in an old outbuilding: rough whitewashed lime plaster over brick, worn timber, old tins and bags - the materials and age to paint from. Image 3 is our finished painting of Mira's property from the street: the red-brick workshop with its weathered plank door on the brick-paved pavement, the stone walls and hedges of the street - this is what is seen outside through the open outer door. The interior is invented.

Brief: a separate, unused building with an outside entrance: old suitcases, a shelf with school teaching aids, a locked case on a table. Beyond an opening there is a further workshop room. Thursday 29 October 2020, afternoon: warm low sunlight falls in through the open outer door at the left, a long sunbeam on the floorboards with dust motes; a soft blue glow comes out of the doorway at the right.

Camera: standing inside the room, about 2.2 m high, looking straight at its long back wall, which is parallel to the picture and fills the whole picture up to the top edge - the ceiling is NOT visible, only one heavy dark timber beam along the very top edge; no side walls. Vertical lines stay vertical. Keep this exact geometry from the sketch (the camera stays this far from the wall, do not move closer): the wall meets the floor at y 790 (73 % from the top) along the whole width, with a dark skirting; the outer door opening x 40-270, y 356-790; the inner doorway x 1646-1876, y 356-790; the table top at y 606 (56 %); the shelving unit from y 306 to the floor; the floorboards from y 790 to the bottom edge are empty. Everything stands against the wall with its feet at y 790-800.

What the sketch blocks are, left to right: the open outer door in a dark weathered timber frame, bright sunny daylight outside: the red-brick pavement, the neighbour's whitewashed stone wall across the street with a hedge and a yellow tree above it; a bare light bulb hanging on a cord from the beam; the whitewashed wall with patches of bare red brick and a greenish damp stain; the worn wooden table against the wall; three old suitcases stacked on the floor at the wall (brown leather, a smaller one, a little grey-blue one on top); three old wooden skis with curled tips leaning on the wall; the tall old wooden shelving unit full of school teaching aids (rolled wall maps, an abacus, chalk boxes, old school books, a microscope, a botanical model, wooden geometry shapes); the inner doorway in a timber frame into the dim back room, where a round frame on the far wall glows soft blue; the worn wide pine floorboards.

Interactive props - each painted clearly inside its block, the same size as its block, easy to recognise at a glance:
1. the block of the layout sketch at x 425-609, y 505-613 of the 1920x1080 frame (22-32 % from the left, 47-57 % from the top): a closed, old brass instrument case with a leather handle, a small engraved bell emblem on the lid and a brass clasp, lying on the worn wooden table.
2. the block of the layout sketch at x 1022-1140, y 305-793 of the 1920x1080 frame (53-59 % from the left, 28-73 % from the top): exactly three old wooden skis with curled tips and old cable bindings, leaning side by side on the wall.
3. the block of the layout sketch at x 1292-1440, y 178-316 of the 1920x1080 frame (67-75 % from the left, 16-29 % from the top): an old school globe with a brass meridian on a wooden stand, standing on top of the shelving unit.
The open outer door is the area of the layout sketch at x 24-286, y 342-812 of the 1920x1080 frame (1-15 % from the left, 32-75 % from the top); the inner doorway is the area of the layout sketch at x 1630-1892, y 342-812 of the 1920x1080 frame (85-99 % from the left, 32-75 % from the top).

Walkable floor: the band at x 20-1900, y 812-1015 of the 1920x1080 frame (1-99 % from the left, 75-94 % from the top) is the worn wide pine floorboard floor - one continuous flat surface with no step, no rug and no threshold inside it, and nothing standing on it: no buckets, no boxes, no tools, no watering can, no people. Only light, the sunbeam from the door, dust and a few dry leaves blown in.
This room has no NPC zones.

Fiction rules: invented interior; no brands on tins, boxes or books, no readable text anywhere (book spines and labels blank, the case shows only a bell emblem), no house numbers. No people, no animals.

The layout sketch is a blocking aid only: paint over all of it. Do NOT draw frames, borders, outlines or boxes around objects, and keep no flat colour block. The finished picture contains no UI, no captions, no text except what is asked for above, no watermark and no people or animals unless stated above.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
